_comment: Known, accepted divergences between a firmware pin table and a datasheet.
One firmware table serves a whole MCU family, but a datasheet describes one
part. Where two parts of a family genuinely differ, no single table can
satisfy both datasheets and the audit is permanently red on one of them - and
a check that can never go green stops being read.
A waiver silences one exact (peripheral, signal, pin, datasheet) finding and
nothing else. It does NOT suppress a category. If firmware changes so the
waived finding no longer occurs, the waiver is reported as stale and the run
still fails: a waiver that has quietly stopped applying is as much a problem
Every entry needs a reason a reviewer can check. 'known issue' is not one.

waivers.reason: Valid on STM32G473 (DS12712 Rev 5, Table 13: PA10 AF2 = I2C3_SCL) but not on STM32G474 (DS12288 Rev 6, where PA10 AF2 is empty and I2C3_SCL is PA8). The STM32G474 target serves boards built on either part, so the entry has to stay for G473 boards.
waivers.verified: 2026-07-31, read from the rendered AF tables of both datasheets

waivers.reason: Valid on STM32G474 (DS12288 Rev 6, Table 13: PA13 AF4 = I2C1_SCL) but absent from the STM32G473 datasheet (DS12712 Rev 5). Shared target, so the entry stays for G474 boards.
waivers.verified: 2026-07-31, read from the rendered AF tables of both datasheets

waivers.reason: As above: PA13 AF3 = I2C4_SCL on STM32G474, absent on STM32G473.
